chunks: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Musa ibn Bakr, from Zurara, who said:

When she looks [for her menstrual cycle], and she does not find the pure periods (al-aqra') except for three months, so if her menstruation is not regular for her, she menstruates multiple times in the month, then her waiting period is the waiting period of the one suffering from irregular bleeding (al-mustahadha), which is three months; and if she menstruates a regular menstruation, then it is one menstruation in each month, with a month between every two menstruations, and that is the pure period (al-quroo).

key_terms.الْأَقْرَاءَ: The pure periods (plural of quroo) in which a woman is free from menstruation
key_terms.الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ: The woman suffering from irregular uterine bleeding

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a woman with irregular menstruation who cannot establish a regular cycle?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between a woman with irregular menstruation (mustahadha) and one with a regular cycle, establishing that the absence of three consecutive months of regularity triggers the three-month waiting period rule. It further defines the 'quroo' (period of purity) as the interval between monthly cycles, a key concept in Shia fiqh for determining iddah duration. This ruling reflects the Imams' practical approach to resolving ambiguity in menstrual patterns, ensuring legal certainty for divorce and inheritance matters.

en.hubeali: Muhammad, from Ahmad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Musa Bin Bakr, from Zurara who said,

‘When she looks, so she does not find the Quroos (pure periods) except for three months, so it was such that her menstruations were not regular for her, she being menstruating time and again during the month, so her waiting period is the waiting period of the one suffering from vaginal bleeding, three months; and when it was such that her menstruations were regular menstruations, so it is one menstruation during each month, between every two menstruations being a month, and that is the Quroo (pure period)’.
en.sarwar: 10. Muhammad has narrated from Ahmad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Musa ibn Bakr from Zurarah who has said the following: “He (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

If she waits and does not find the Hayd (menses)-free period except three months then if her Hayd (menses) is not straight. If she experiences Hayd in a month several times such woman’s waiting period is like the waiting period of one who experiences Istihadah, whose ‘Iddah (waiting period) is three months. If she experiences Hayd straightly, thus, in every month is one Hayd and between two Hayd (menses) one month of time it is the Hayd-free period.’”
